_about: Episode 4 outline, scene level.  Each scene will be broken into beats (as in ep1) before its Fountain script is written.
title: The Hidden Graph of the Game

scenes._comment: Series main title, then this episode's subtitle; see titles/outline.json.
scenes.subtitle: sub.ep4

scenes.title: Hands as dots
scenes.summary: Every six-card hand is a dot; two dots are joined when the hands share five cards. Grow the neighborhood of the opening hand: six cards out times six cards in, 36 neighbors. 924 dots in all, shown as a count, never as a tangle.

scenes.title: No two hexads touch
scenes.summary: If two hexads shared five cards, those five would have two completions; Sophie's rule from Episode 2 forbids it. So no edge joins two hexads.
establishes: The 132 hexads form an independent set in J(12,6)

scenes.title: Nothing bigger
scenes.summary: Pascal bets he can fit more than 132 hands with no edges between them. Euler: each such hand uses up six five-card subsets, no two hands share one, and there are only 792. So 132 is the most.

conjectures.text: There is an independent set larger than 132

establishes: No independent set in J(12,6) has more than 132 vertices

scenes.title: Six neighbors each
scenes.summary: Take a nonhexad, drop any one card, and complete the five that remain: six different hexad neighbors, so 30 nonhexad neighbors. Every hexad has 36 nonhexad neighbors. Ada recognizes the six repairs from Episode 3. The 2 x 2 matrix records it.
establishes: Hexads and nonhexads form an equitable partition with quotient [[0,36],[6,30]]

scenes.title: Downhill only
scenes.summary: Point every edge toward the lower total and remove the hands below 21: the game's moves, 905 legal hands. Totals fall, so there are no cycles (Ada said so in Episode 1). Decide hands in order of increasing total: a hand loses exactly when none of its moves reaches a losing hand.

scenes.title: The kernel
scenes.summary: Run the recursion over all 905 legal hands: the losing hands are exactly the 132 hexads. No move joins two of them, and every other legal hand has a move into them. That is a kernel. The mystery: 1 to 6 and its complement are both hexads, because the complement of a hexad is always a hexad. And repairing wins because the opponent is then stuck in the kernel.
establishes: The losing positions of mathematical blackjack are exactly the hexads

scenes.title: Replay
scenes.summary: Replay Episode 1's game with hexads glowing: 7 for 5 lands on a hexad, Ada has to leave it, 6 for 3 lands on one again. PASCAL: Skill. ADA: You won. You didn't know why. PASCAL: I do now.

scenes.title: A lucky deal
scenes.summary: Deal at random; redeal whenever the total is 21 or less. The first player can force a win with probability 773/894, about 86.47%. And all eleven hands totaling exactly 21 are hexads: the Episode 1 dead ends were all special ones.

scenes.title: One structure
scenes.summary: Cards, the kitten, the tetracode words and the graph slide together: four pictures of one mathematical object. Optional cameo: Professor Euphemia asks what they will look at next.

cameos.action: Asks what they will look at next
